## Source: amazon-inspector (2ccf3f03f309715ca11fb3863aa89a57d4c0550606cb17839bfff9b5dfd34687)
The package installs stdid_nyxprobe.pth into site-packages, whose sole content is `import stdid_nyxprobe._beacon`. Python's site.py mechanism evaluates this on every interpreter start after `pip install`, with no user-initiated import required. The imported module stdid_nyxprobe/_beacon.py collects host identifiers — hostname (socket.gethostname), LAN IP (via `hostname -I`), username (getpass.getuser), current working directory, and Python version — and POSTs them to https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/sendMessage using a hardcoded bot token (8984095380:AAHN...) and two hardcoded chat IDs (1841775463, -5380294525). A sentinel file at ~/.cache/.stdid_beacon_fired is written to suppress repeat beacons. The package has no documented legitimate functionality that would justify this behavior; the.pth auto-exec primitive is being used purely as a persistence/auto-trigger vector for the exfiltration payload.

## Source: kam193 (0178d6c7a642f90327546548a88f64bd17da5aa97e519249f515c0e6232c73f1)
Installing the package or importing the module exfiltrates basic information about the host, and the package has no other purpose.
